title: The interaction contract
prompt:
Implement `MailerSpy` and `send_welcome(mailer, user)`:

- MailerSpy: `send(to, subject, body)` records the call and returns True; if `fail_next` is set, it raises `ConnectionError` once (and clears the flag) instead
- `send_welcome`: sends `('Welcome!', 'Hi <name>')` to `user['email']`; returns True on success, False when the mailer raised `ConnectionError` — and on failure it must NOT retry inside the call

The spy makes the contract observable: exactly one send on success, exactly zero on failure.

tests.name: one send on success, zero on failure
tests.code:
spy = MailerSpy()
assert send_welcome(spy, {'email': 'a@x.y', 'name': 'Lan'}) is True
assert spy.sent == [{'to': 'a@x.y', 'subject': 'Welcome!', 'body': 'Hi Lan'}]
spy.fail_next = True
assert send_welcome(spy, {'email': 'b@x.y', 'name': 'Minh'}) is False
assert len(spy.sent) == 1  # the failed attempt recorded nothing, and did not loop
print('ok')
tests.hint: Failure surfaces as a return value, not an infinite retry.
